note: Append-only. Entries are added; none are edited or deleted. Times are UTC (ET = UTC-5 tonight). Scope patterns: '*' every race; 'ST' two-letter state; 'house:GA-*' prefix; 'src:added' source; exact race key; 'national' = not tied to a race.

incidents.what: From 01:32Z (9:32 pm ET) the registered House model stopped updating Georgia districts: a parse TypeError in the registered code. Georgia House rows after that time are stale. Not fixed as of this entry.
incidents.effect_on_model: Georgia House counted/share/P values stay at their 01:32Z reading (e.g. GA-12 counted 51.62%) while only the market columns keep moving. They do not reflect later counting.
incidents.evidence: Operator report of the TypeError; log rows: GA-12 in registered-house.jsonl shows counted 0.5162 unchanged from 01:32Z. The rows are not flagged stale in the feed itself.

incidents.scope_text: South Carolina (registered models and civic fallback)
incidents.what: The official South Carolina results feed was blocked for the whole night, so the registered SC models read 0% counted. The civicAPI secondary models were used as a fallback. The civic SC Senate count stuck at 36.2% from about 01:25Z. (Start time approximate.)
incidents.effect_on_model: Registered SC Senate/governor models show 0% counted and are not informed by the count. Civic SC models use civicAPI counts, which were stuck at 36.18% (SC Senate) from 01:25Z until about 03:12Z, when it jumped to 90.1%.
incidents.evidence: Log rows: sc-sen (registered) counted 0.0; sc-sen-civic counted 0.3618 from 01:25Z to ~03:00Z and 0.9012 from 03:12Z.
incidents.correction: The start time is approximate (poll close); the exact first occurrence was not recorded.

incidents.what: Ohio's official results feed returned HTTP 429 (too many requests) from 00:13Z (7:13 pm ET); recovered by about 03:00Z (10:00 pm ET).
incidents.effect_on_model: Ohio counts were not updating during the gap; model readings in that window carry the last count that was received.
incidents.evidence: Operator report of the 429 responses; see Ohio rows' counted over the window.
incidents.correction: Sourced times from the monitor log (alerts_new.log): first HTTP 429 from liveresults.ohiosos.gov at 00:13Z. The monitor showed the feed CLEARED at 02:17Z/02:19Z and a new problem again at 02:25Z. The registered Ohio model was counting again (57% counted) by about 02:58Z. The earlier end time of 03:00Z was approximate.

incidents.scope_text: Virginia House (added model), VA-01 most visibly
incidents.what: The added-source Virginia parser read an incomplete state file as zero votes at 03:20:50Z and again at 03:44:54Z (10:20 pm and 10:44 pm ET). Each time the VA-01 projection was withdrawn (count reset to 0%, P back near the prior). Fixed in commit fb24c61, deployed about 03:50Z.
incidents.effect_on_model: VA-01 showed two false resets on the public page (03:21Z and 03:45Z). The rebuilt history after the restart no longer shows them, because the service rebuilds from recorded files with the fixed code. The as-published rows are included in this log as 'captured-live'.
incidents.evidence: Rows with recorded='captured-live' for house:VA-01 in added-house.jsonl, read from the live tunnel at ~03:46Z before the restart.

incidents.what: The added-source service was restarted several times tonight, most recently about 03:50Z for fix fb24c61. Each restart rebuilds its history from recorded files using the current code, so the added-source history in this log (recorded='backfilled') may differ from what the public page showed at the time. The registered sources were never restarted tonight; their backfill is still tagged 'backfilled'.
incidents.effect_on_model: Added-source history before the last restart is a re-computation, not a contemporaneous reading. Only rows tagged 'live' or 'captured-live' were recorded as published.
incidents.evidence: recorded and rebuilt_from fields on every row of the log.

incidents.what: The added Virginia model reported a spread of about 0.0005 (a vote-share standard deviation of 0.05 points) while batches were still outstanding, so P went to 0 or 1 on small count moves.
incidents.effect_on_model: VA P values near 0.00 or 1.00 are overconfident; the model's stated uncertainty was too small.
incidents.evidence: VA-01 rows: sd 0.0005 with P 0.0 and 1.0 on consecutive minutes (02:46Z and 02:47Z).

incidents.scope_text: Florida, Nebraska, South Carolina, Ohio, New Hampshire, civic and added models
incidents.what: These models have no early-ballot versus Election-Day split, so early-ballot counts read as a swing to the Democrat. (Start time approximate.)
incidents.effect_on_model: Early projections in states that count early ballots first are biased toward the Democrat and drift back as Election-Day votes arrive.
incidents.evidence: Model design; compare raw (share counted) with projected share in the rows.
incidents.correction: The start time is approximate (poll close); the exact first occurrence was not recorded.

incidents.scope_text: North Carolina, Georgia, Texas, Arizona House (split models)
incidents.what: The early/Election-Day split House models for NC, GA, TX and AZ were calibrated on 2024. Tonight's early-versus-Election-Day gap in North Carolina is about 15-17 points, which the models under-correct.
incidents.effect_on_model: NC-05 and NC-07 model P is too Democratic. Other NC/GA/TX/AZ House readings may lean the same way.
incidents.evidence: Operator analysis of the NC early vs Election-Day count gap; see NC-05 and NC-07 rows.
incidents.correction: Sourced evidence, 02:30-02:50Z: the NC-07 early-versus-Election-Day gap was 15.5 points and NC-05 13.3 points (the 2024 calibration had 0-4). Election-Day counted votes were 27% D in NC-05 and 29% D in NC-07, against an implied remaining 47-53%. The earlier start time of 00:30Z was a guess.

incidents.what: One-sided Polymarket order books read inverted: for example the Florida governor pm value was 0.999 at about 03:15Z while Donalds (R) leads. 102 of 353 books were one-sided.
incidents.effect_on_model: Polymarket values (the pm column) on such races are not market consensus. Use with care; Kalshi is shown alongside where available.
incidents.correction: The 102-of-353 count is from our edge feed at 01:35Z (it is not a night-long figure). The start time is when it was observed, not when the books first went one-sided.

incidents.scope_text: National seat count (not a single race)
incidents.what: The early-signal adjusted seat line was paused at commit 5820051 because of a count-order bias. (Time shown is when this entry was written; the exact pause time was not recorded.)
incidents.effect_on_model: No effect on race rows in this log; the national seat line is not logged here.
incidents.correction: The pause time is commit 5820051 at 01:19:18Z. The first version of this entry used the time the entry was written (03:52Z).

incidents.what: The models overreacted to the earliest counts: with 0.33% counted in Minnesota, the governor model P moved from 71% to 38%.
incidents.effect_on_model: Minnesota and Wisconsin projections during the first few percent counted are unreliable.
incidents.evidence: mn-gov rows at the first counted values.
incidents.correction: Sourced figures: registered mn-gov at 02:40Z had 0.33% counted (about 8,000 votes) and P 0.382 against 0.7118 pre-count; mn-sen P was 0.304; markets were at 98-99%. WI civic at 02:33Z had 8.6% counted and P 0.333 against a market of 0.965. Start time moved from the 02:00Z poll close to the first of these readings.

incidents.what: This log was started at 03:52Z. Rows before the first live row in each file were rebuilt afterwards from the server's timeline files, only keeping rows where a published value changed. They are tagged 'backfilled'.
incidents.effect_on_model: Backfilled rows may differ from what the page showed at the time (see the restart incident).
